title: Coefficients of low degree truncation
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $S\subseteq[n]$. Then $\widehat{f^{\le k}}(S)=\widehat f(S)$ if $|S|\le k$, and zero otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on the n-dimensional cube
k is a natural number (truncation level)
S is an arbitrary subset of [n]
replaced:
The truncation acts as a projection on the Fourier side: for every $S$,
$\widehat{f_{\le k}}(S) = \hat f(S)$ when $\abs{S} \le k$, and
$\widehat{f_{\le k}}(S) = 0$ otherwise.
